title: Which of the six simplified cards hide a mistake?
description: Six simplified expressions from the book are checked one by one, each mistake is named, and the correct expression is written. Keeko then doubts the card on the square of a sum and squares each term, which drops the middle term.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiply every term by every term, add only like terms, and keep the middle term of a square. Watch for students who square each term of a sum and leave out the middle term.

source: Mind the Mistake, Mend the Mistake (the first six cards)
video_script.why: The child can expand a bracket and a square, but has not yet used those rules to find the slip in someone else's working.
video_script.substitution: Check each card by multiplying every term by every term, then say what went wrong and write the correct expression, as the book asks.
video_script.anchor: the six simplified cards from the book, one expression on each card
video_script.wrong_answer: twenty five m squared plus thirty six n squared
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko squares each term of five m plus six n, and drops the middle term. With m and n both one, that gives sixty one instead of one hundred twenty one.
video_script.payoff_line: Five cards had a mistake, and only card five was correct.

final_answer.spoken: five cards had a mistake, and only card five was correct

video_script.design: One idea: check each card by multiplying every term by every term. The cards stay on the board in a grid and each is mended in place. Keeko's wrong idea is to square each term of a sum.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; six cards in a grid, each with a short working line: -3p(-5p + 2q) = p - 2q, 2(x - 1) + 3(x + 4) = 5x + 3, y + 2(y + 2) = y² + 4y + 4, (5m + 6n)² = 25m² + 36n², (-q + 2)² = q² - 4q + 4, 3a(2b × 3c) = 54a²bc

<bookmark mark='cards'/>It shows six cards, and someone simplified each one of them.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is every card right, or do some of them hide a mistake?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='tasks'/>Your book asks three things for each card. Check it, say what went wrong, and write the correct expression.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the six cards from your book.

beats.on_screen: To find: the mistake in each card, and the correct expression

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the mistake in each card, and mend it.

marks.one: card 1: -3p is multiplied into both terms of the bracket

beats.colours: the two multipliers in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, card one. Minus three p must multiply both terms in the bracket.
<bookmark mark='one2'/>Minus three p times minus five p is fifteen p squared. Minus three p times two q is minus six p q.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Card two. The two and the three must multiply the second terms too, which gives five x plus ten.

marks.four: card 4: the middle term 2 × 5m × 6n = 60mn is written in the accent colour

beats.colours: the middle term in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step two, card three. It is a sum, not a square. Y plus two y plus four makes three y plus four.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Card four has its middle term missing. Twice five m times six n is sixty m n.
<bookmark mark='four2'/>The correct line is twenty five m squared plus sixty m n plus thirty six n squared.

marks.five: card 5: (-q + 2)² = q² - 4q + 4 is written and ticked
marks.six2: 3a × 6bc is written, not yet worked out

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step three, card five. It is correct, because minus q plus two all squared gives q squared minus four q plus four.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Card six. Two b times three c is one multiplication, six b c.
<bookmark mark='six2'/>Then multiply that by three eigh.

marks.ans: the six corrected lines are written and boxed
marks.list1: the first three corrected lines light up
marks.list2: 3a × 6bc = 18abc is written, and the last two lines light up

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Five cards had a mistake, and only card five was correct.
<bookmark mark='list1'/>Card one is fifteen p squared minus six p q. Card two is five x plus ten. Card three is three y plus four.
<bookmark mark='list2'/>Card four is twenty five m squared plus sixty m n plus thirty six n squared. Card six is eighteen eigh b c.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the answer line
beats.removed: the working lines fade to the answer line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: (5m + 6n)² = 25m² + 36n²; test with m = 1, n = 1: (5 + 6)² = 121 and 25 + 36 = 61; the bubble is struck in the warning colour

marks.test: m = 1 and n = 1 are written, and (5 + 6)² = 121 appears
marks.fix: the bubble is struck in the warning colour
marks.mid: 60mn lights up as the missing term

beats.colours: the wrong line in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks card four was right, because each term was squared. That gives twenty five m squared plus thirty six n squared.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Test it with m and n both one. Five plus six is eleven, and eleven squared is one hundred twenty one.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>Keeko's line gives only twenty five plus thirty six, which is sixty one.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The two answers do not match, which means the line is wrong.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>The sixty m n term is missing, and it fills the gap.
